plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green, palmate leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions and is prized for flowering in the depths of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy 'flowers' are actually colorful bracts surrounding small yellow cyathia. Outdoors in warm climates it can reach several meters in height, while elsewhere it is a popular potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in frost-free regions such as Southern California, Florida, Hawaii and Australia, and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias need long nights of about 12 to 14 hours of uninterrupted darkness for several weeks to trigger their colorful bracts, which is why they bloom around December.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flat, segmented, claw-edged stems and pendant, zygomorphic flowers that appear at the stem tips. In nature it grows in tree branches and rock crevices in humid forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, this species lives in humid, shady forests, and it sets flower buds in response to cool temperatures and long nights.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with feathery, fern-like leaves that erupts in dense clusters of large, vivid flowers. It is among the most spectacular flowering trees of the tropics and subtropics.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); flowering varies in the tropics depending on the dry season
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in the tropics and subtropics including Brazil, northern Australia, South Africa, India and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: In the wild in Madagascar the species is endangered, even though it is one of the most commonly planted ornamental trees in the world.
